0: Every run starts with a task. In a debate all the debaters get the same question, and each has a side.
1: The first Debater argues for later start times. Debaters speak one at a time, not at the same time.
3: The first argument. It goes into the transcript that the next Debater will read.
4: A handoff records the turn for the Judge, who reads everything at the end.
5: The second Debater argues against. Its input holds the first argument, so it can answer it.
7: The second argument answers the first point by point, instead of just repeating its own side.
9: The Judge starts only after all rounds are done. With one round, that is right after the second Debater.
11: The verdict: which side argued better and why. It becomes the final answer.
12: The run ends. The final answer is the Judge's verdict.
